title: Why copy-paste gets painful
idea: You could repeat a step by copying a line many times — but it is slow, error-prone, and breaks when the count changes. That pain is why loops exist.

exercises.prompt: To show Hi five times, a beginner writes print("Hi") five times. What is the main downside?
options: If the count changes to 50, you must copy 50 lines
It will not run at all
exercises.explanation: Copy-paste works for 5 but is miserable for 50 or 500. Loops let one line stand in for many.

exercises.prompt: Copying the same line many times is easy to get wrong (a typo in one copy).
exercises.explanation: Every copy is a chance for a mistake. One looped line has no copies to get out of sync.

exercises.prompt: You pasted print("Hi") 10 times but one line says print("Hii"). What happens?
options: One line shows Hii instead of Hi
exercises.explanation: Only the mistyped copy is wrong. Hunting one bad copy among ten is exactly the pain loops remove.

exercises.prompt: Which situation makes copy-paste repetition clearly a bad idea?
exercises.explanation: 1000 copies is unthinkable by hand. The bigger the count, the more you want a loop.

exercises.prompt: A loop lets you write the repeated step ONCE and choose how many times it runs.
exercises.explanation: That is the whole appeal: one clear step, a count you can change in one place. You'll meet the loop tool soon.

exercises.prompt: With copy-paste, to change Hi to Hello everywhere, you must...
exercises.explanation: Change in many copies = many edits and easy mistakes. A loop changes the body in one place.

exercises.prompt: Order these reasons from the problem to the fix.
blocks: Copy-paste means many lines and many mistakes
A step needs to repeat many times
A loop writes the step once and repeats it
exercises.explanation: A step repeats -> copy-paste is painful -> a loop fixes it. That story motivates the whole lap.

exercises.prompt: What is the real benefit of repeating with a loop instead of copies?
options: One place to read, one place to fix, any count
It removes the need to think
exercises.explanation: One readable body, easy to fix, and the count is flexible. That is why every language has loops.

exercises.prompt: For a one-time action, writing it once (no loop) is perfectly fine.
exercises.explanation: Loops are for repetition. If it happens once, just write it once — no loop needed.

exercises.prompt: You see 20 identical print lines in a program. What does that smell like?
options: A repetition that wants to be a loop
exercises.explanation: Twenty identical lines is a loud hint: this is repetition, and a loop would be cleaner. Next units give you that tool.
